query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a secondary phase or grain refinement in single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys will increase the coercive field by pinning of domain walls or reduction of grain size to reduce magnetic domain size.
generation.intervention: Introduction of a secondary phase (e.g., carbides or oxides) or grain refinement (e.g., via mechanical alloying or spark plasma sintering) to create a composite microstructure
generation.structural_mediator: Secondary phase or refined grain structure
generation.mechanism: Pinning of domain walls or reduction of grain size to reduce magnetic domain size, leading to increased coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in coercive field relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, from 100 Oe to 120 Oe
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative
generation.boundary: FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy composition, fcc structure with potential secondary phases or refined grain structure, magnetic measurements at room temperature
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of secondary phase or grain size reduction required to achieve the desired coercive field increase is uncertain, and the potential effects of other microstructural features (e.g., porosity, defects) on coercivity are not well understood.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize and characterize FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with varying secondary phase content or grain sizes, and measure their coercive fields using a vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) or a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometer
measurements: Coercive field (Hc) measurements at room temperature
Microstructural characterization (e.g., X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy) to confirm secondary phase or grain refinement
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the modified alloy is not significantly increased (less than 20% increase, i.e., less than 120 Oe) relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the hypothesis is falsified.
